messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: CRIT - inference-api 5xx rate spike (>40% errors). Incident: PD-112233
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert escalated to primary on-call (Elena). If no ack in 5m, will escalate to secondary (Mike Ops) and manager.
Elena (oncall): ack
Elena (oncall): I'm jumping in, checking logs and recent deploys. TL;DR: high 503s hitting text-generation endpoint /v1/generate.
Sam K: seeing a lot of `UpstreamError: 502` in the gateway logs. Any recent model rollouts?
Elena (oncall): nothing on rollout queue. Prod deploys show a canary for runtime v2.1 ~ 22:10 UTC
Mike Ops: I'm on standby if primary can't keep it. @Elena any mitigation we should try? scale? rollback?
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Primary acknowledged incident PD-112233 (Elena). Monitoring escalation timer.
Elena (oncall): I can repro locally: kv cache warnings + OOM traces on one pool node. Looks like a single GPU pod flapping and taking traffic.
Alex (SRE Lead): Can we cordon the node and let autoscaler replace it? Runbook -> `infra/gpu-pod-flapping`
Elena (oncall): starting cordon/drain on pod `gpu-pool-7a-3` now. `kubectl drain gpu-pool-7a-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Elena (oncall): drain command returned `node not ready`, trying manual delete of pod to force reschedule.
Sam K: logs show `cuda: failed to init` then `OOM in allocator` ~ 22:12:07 UTC. Might be driver crash.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: No ack from primary within 5m. Escalating to secondary: Mike Ops.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Escalation policy fired: paging secondary (Mike Ops) and manager (Jessie).
Mike Ops: ack
Mike Ops: I'm taking over, Elena handoff? what's current mitigation state?
Elena (oncall): I drained the node and deleted flapping pod. Traffic is rebalancing, error rate dropping from 42% -> 12% in 3m.
Mike Ops: good. I'll keep an eye on autoscaler and model runtime processes. If errors drop under 2% we'll close.
Jessie (manager): paging in for visibility. Any customer-facing impact? Which customers saw errors?
Sam K: error traces correlate to high-throughput customers A and C (billing batch jobs), and some flaky small requests. No full outage, degraded for a subset.
Alex (SRE Lead): run quick `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-pool-7a` and check `node-exporter` metrics for driver restarts.
Mike Ops: running check, posting output:
```
NAME                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-gpu-1-7a-3     0/1     CrashLoop 4          2h
inference-gpu-2-7a-4     1/1     Running   0          4h
```
Mike Ops: driver restarted once on that node. I've triggered node remediation and scaled up spare pool by +1 to absorb traffic: `infractl pool scale gpu-pool-7a 4`.
Elena (oncall): error rate stabilizing at ~3.4%. customer A retry logic handled some requests, but we should send an incident note.
Jessie (manager): agree — draft a short customer-facing blurb: impact, mitigation, ETA for full recovery.
Sam K: suggested blurb: "We briefly experienced elevated 5xx errors for the text-generation API affecting a subset of customers processing high-throughput requests. We remediated by draining a flapping GPU node and scaling spare capacity; error rates returned to normal. No data was lost."
Elena (oncall): posting to status page now. I'll also attach graphs and incident link.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD-112233 status updated: acknowledged -> in_progress
Mike Ops: monitoring for 10m then will close if stable. I'll also open a followup ticket for driver investigation and node remediation playbook.
Alex (SRE Lead): create ticket and tag `severity:low` follow-up; include kernel/driver versions and docker image.
Mike Ops: closing note: errors <1% for 12m, autoscaler kept steady capacity, no further flapping. Closing incident.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD-112233 resolved by Mike Ops.
Elena (oncall): thanks all. Postmortem/Eval will be tracked in `incidents/PD-112233` and include detection + missed-ack timeline.
Jessie (manager): thanks team — good handoff. :thumbsup:
